steps.content: You guys wait here.
At the previous stronghold, Hella got into a quarrel with some Legionnaires. Leaving her here to stand guard is clearly the best option.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: As if I want to go!
Hella pouts, but stays as she is told.
You and Horo walk in through the entrance. The interior of the Legion's stronghold comes into view.
As always, everything is made of steel and cement, in line with the Legion's style.
It's just that the building is a bit old.

steps.speaker: Lenny
steps.content: Horo? How come you're here too?

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Lenny, what's the situation?

steps.speaker: Lenny
steps.content: Situation? Oh, you mean those buffoons from the Public Security Bureau.

steps.speaker: Lenny
steps.content: Beaten and fled. No stronghold has been attacked in the past few days. Guess they're probably scared witless.

steps.speaker: Lenny
steps.content: They should know better than to get in our Legion's way. Who do they think they are?
He speaks with an air of triumphant indifference, but his scar-ridden body suggests that he has bitten off more than he can chew.

steps.speaker: Jer
steps.content: ...Come here!
Another Legionnaire named Jer pulls you to the side.

steps.speaker: Jer
steps.content: Why did you bring Horo here? Aren't you supposed to be protecting her?
As you can see, I am protecting her.

steps.speaker: Jer
steps.content: You think you're protecting her by bringing her back to this Syndicate war zone? Have you forgotten your promise to Boss Zoya?!
Horo and I made this decision together.
We are looking for information left by Earl.
Jer's face sinks at the mention of Earl's name.
As long as we find the right records, the 9th Agency will have a reason to get involved and sweep up the remnants of the Public Security Bureau.
Horo's safety and the threats faced by the Legion will all be resolved in one go.

steps.speaker: Jer
steps.content: Cut the bullcrap! Aside from you, I don't trust any of those Eastside bastards!
The shouts catch Horo's attention. Jer quickly lowers his voice again.

steps.speaker: Jer
steps.content: Fine. At least I trust Horo. Those two kids... I watched them grow up.

steps.speaker: Jer
steps.content: Earl's room is 301, but he didn't leave much there. You can look for it yourself.
You enter Room 301 together. After many minutes of searching, you still find nothing of use.
...It's not here either.
Horo frowns, pondering other possible places.
We already visited all the Legion strongholds mentioned earlier. Where else could the records be hidden?

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: ...The only place left is the trailer park.

steps.speaker: Lenny
steps.content: The trailer park? Hasn't that been abandoned long ago?

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: After the Convoy left, Earl and I continued to live there for two years.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: After some... misunderstandings, I never went back. But Earl still goes there from time to time.
Is it a well-hidden place?

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Sort of. I mean, hardly anyone goes there now, since all the valuables have been looted long ago.
Great place for a secret hideout, no?
Horo nods.
No time to waste. Let's go.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Okay.

steps.speaker: Jer
steps.content: Hold on.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Jer?

steps.speaker: Jer
steps.content: You've been wandering in Syndicate for a while now. Some spies might have noticed you.

steps.speaker: Jer
steps.content: Lenny, Danny, Kevin, come. Let's go together.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: What about the defense of the stronghold?

steps.speaker: Jer
steps.content: There hasn't been an attack for days. And it's only 20 minutes to the old trailer park from here. We shouldn't be that unlucky.

steps.speaker: Jer
steps.content: Plus their target is ultimately you. So I'm worried...
Jer looks to Horo with concern in his eyes.
Horo looks back at you, as if seeking your opinion.
...Let's go together then.
You sigh somewhat helplessly.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: This is some ****ing shabby place.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: And that stench... How can anyone live here?

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Hey lil' bitty, now I get why you didn't come back for so long. That Earl...

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Hella...
Hecate hisses at Hella, who realizes she has said something she shouldn't have. She purses her lips and doesn't speak again.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Up ahead.
Horo doesn't seem to care. Under her guidance, the group comes to a rusty trailer.
Horo walks up to the trailer door, kicks the lower left corner, shakes the door handle roughly a few times, then pushes it hard.
The door opens with a nauseating creak.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: That's some way to open a door...
Unlike its rusty, run-down exterior, the inside of the trailer is meticulously maintained, complete with a full kitchen set that is old but well-polished.
The succulents on the windowsill are lush and green, having obviously been watered by their owner not long ago.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: The room is on the left.
Horo utters a reminder.
Inside the room, there is a bunk bed, as well as stacks of papers piled up around a desk.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ...I'm heading out. I won't be much help here anyways.
Hella pulls Hecate out of the trailer.
You, Horo, and several other team members begin to read the information in front of you.
An hour passes, and more than half of Earl's records have been filtered out. Yet you still haven't found the information you're looking for.
Horo seems a bit absent-minded all this time.
Horo.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Yes?
Horo's mind has wandered again.
You understand how she feels. Her brother just died, and this place is full of his memories. It would be extremely difficult to keep calm.
Let's take a break.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: ...Okay.
Horo, realizing that she'll only slow down the progress in her current state, silently leaves the room.
You follow her.
Don't be too sad...
You think for a long time, yet you fail to find anything useful to say.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: I told you, I'm not a child.
I understand how you feel.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: You've also lost someone dear to you before?
You are taken aback by Horo's sudden response.
Horo's lips gently curl into a bitter smile.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: You're just like my brother. Too clumsy to even comfort people.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: You're lucky to have not experienced anything like this...

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: But I've experienced it, over and over again. I can remember everything so clearly...

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: After Mom and Dad left, I lived here with my brother.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: He was our breadwinner. He would always teach the boys who bullied me a good lesson. No one in the mean streets could beat him.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: He was really amazing.
Horo caresses the dining table, where two sets of cutlery are neatly arranged.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Later, he joined the Convoy. He was doing two men's work and dead tired when he came home every day.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: I felt really bad, but I didn't know what I could do, so I just watched.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: One day, some men from the Convoy carried him back home. He had lost a leg.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: I was so scared that he would leave me just like Mom and Dad did.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: The pain kept him awake all night, and I cried the whole night next to him. Yet there was still nothing I could do to help. I didn't know how to handle his wound, I couldn't comfort him, and I couldn't relieve his pain.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: That day was when I realized I must grow up quickly to help him.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: So I joined the Convoy too. And later, the Convoy became the Legion.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: But the harder I tried to prove myself, the more he tried to stop me.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: He always thought that I was just a little kid who should hide behind him, and that he should shoulder everything himself.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: I was so mad. The madder I got, the more I argued with him. In the end, I stopped talking to him altogether.
Horo wipes her eyes with her arm.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: ${PlayerName}, I'm so stupid.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: He was the dearest family to me, yet I couldn't even speak properly to him.
Tears stream out from her reddened eyes. Her emotions that has been pent up for many days are finally gushing out.
After a while, her sobs slowly subside.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Earl is dead.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: I can't be the little kid who hides behind him anymore.
Horo wipes away her tears and flashes a heart-wrenching smile.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: I'm sorry, ${PlayerName}. I must be boring you with my rant.
Of course not.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: ...I just remembered that my brother has a bad habit of hiding things.
Horo goes back into the study and pulls open the desk drawers. She pries open the bottom plates one by one, revealing a few notebooks.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: I knew it. He used to love hiding things in these places.
Horo rummages for a while and flips open one of the notebooks. Her eyes are still a bit red, but her expression is calm and determined.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: D'Artagnan, Bliss, Massi... I remember these names.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: These are the people the Public Security Bureau dealt with.
You take the notebook. It contains records of the aforementioned people's dealings with the Public Security Bureau, and the destruction of Mania weapons.
As long as the locations in this file are found, it would be enough to convict those in the Public Security Bureau—but that's the 9th Agency's job.
Your work here is done.

steps.speaker: Mission Operative
steps.content: If Earl had given this to the Chief earlier... Things wouldn't have gotten to this.
One of the mission operatives expresses regret.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Regret is meaningless.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Plus, there was no way my brother could trust you back then.

steps.speaker: Mission Operative
steps.content: Then at least he should have told someone else.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: The Legion has enough enemies as it is. It would've only added to everyone's burden.
You don't know from when, but Horo has started to think like Earl and Zoya.
After confirming the information, you send messages to the MBCC and the 9th Agency.

options: Get the team together and retreat ASAP

choices.text: Get the team together and retreat ASAP

steps.content: Everyone heeds your order and quickly leaves the trailer after sorting out the materials that need to be taken away.
Only Horo looks back longingly.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: I'll be back... But for now, it's time to say goodbye...
Boom!
An explosion nearby interrupts the sentimental farewell.
After a few gunshots, Hella rushes back with Lenny.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Why are you still dilly-dallying here? The Public Security Bureau forces are here!
Hella pants heavily as Hecate explains the situation.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: There's more than a hundred of them, and they have Mania weapons.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: We're surrounded.
